title: cascade-allocation-with-bounded-fragmentation-controller
creator: Marcus Chen
description:
Problem: GPU-resident KV cache exhibits slow-but-steady fragmentation under continuous-batching workloads. Fragmentation increases per-model memory footprint and causes periodic hot OOMs during bursty traffic. Goal: implement a low-latency, low-overhead allocation & compaction strategy that bounds fragmentation while preserving inference latency SLOs.

Proposal (high level): introduce a cascade allocation policy plus a bounded compaction controller. Key ideas: a) allocate new KV slots from small 'micro-heaps' (per-worker, per-model) to localize churn, b) maintain soft partitions with yearly-style aging (token TTL + churn score) to guide compaction candidates, c) run cooperative incremental compaction across workers using epoch markers and non-blocking copy-on-write for live KV relocation, and d) schedule compaction work using a cost-aware scheduler that respects per-request latency budget and GPU occupancy.

Why unique: instead of global stop-the-world defrag or aggressive slab coalescing, this approach treats fragmentation as an operational signal and amortizes healing over typical idle windows. It tightly integrates with the continuous-batching runtime to piggyback KV movements onto normal token generation boundaries so per-request latency impact is bounded.
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation ratio (wasted bytes / allocated bytes) reduces by >= 60% on representative RLHF and chat workloads within 24 hours of deployment
99th percentile generation latency increase <= 5% under steady-state load when compaction background work is enabled
No new OOM incidents caused by compaction in 7-day canary across three clusters
Telemetry surfaces compaction cost per model and per GPU with sampleable traces
Feature toggle to fully disable compaction per-customer and a rollout plan through console

technical_notes: Micro-heap: fixed-size per-worker slab segments (4k/16k/64k classes) allocated from pooled device memory to reduce cross-worker fragmentation
Cascade: allocate from smallest micro-heap first; upon saturation, allocate from larger local pool; fall back to global pool only when needed
Compaction: use copy-on-write relocation that updates KV indirection table atomically to avoid pausing token generation; relocation occurs at batch boundaries
Scheduler: cost model uses recent token churn rate, GPU utilization, and 95th latency slack to decide compaction quantum
Safety: compaction quantum per-GPU capped (bytes/sec) and backed off when per-request latency approaches target
Coordination: light-weight epoch numbers embedded in request tracing to ensure relocation visibility for all workers
Telemetry: per-model fragmentation, bytes_moved, compaction_time_ms, cpu_cycles_used and latency_delta tagged by model-version and pool
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Non-blocking relocation is prioritized over throughput of compaction; this reduces maximum fragmentation speed but avoids SLO violations
Micro-heaps increase allocator metadata but reduce cross-talk fragmentation — small memory overhead (approx 1-3% of total KV memory) acceptable given benefits
Aggressive global compaction would yield lower fragmentation faster but risks latency spikes; chosen bounded approach prefers operational stability
Scheduler complexity vs ease-of-operation: we implement a simple cost model now and leave ML-driven scheduling for follow-up
We avoid hardware-specific kernel hacks initially to keep code portable across NV and AMD GPUs; future PRs may introduce optimized kernels

2026-02-18: Prototype micro-heap allocator completed on branch feat/kv-microheap; unit tests for allocation/deallocation added. Locally reduces fragmentation by ~30% on synthetic churn workload.
2026-02-25: Implemented epoch coordinator and basic relocation API; integration tests show no pauses during relocation when churn < 40%.
2026-03-03: First internal canary on 2 GPUs: observed 10% increase in background CPU cycles but 2% 99th latency increase; adjusted scheduler quantum down 40%.
2026-03-08: Observability hooks merged: compaction events, bytes_moved, and per-model fragmentation metric available in dev dashboards (internal Grafana link).
2026-03-10: Preparing broader staging canary (5 GPUs) and production rollout plan; created feature toggle and per-customer opt-out via runtime config
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator invariants and atomic indirection updates
Integration tests with continuous-batching harness to validate no request-level stalls
Load tests: simulated chat bursts (10x baseline), RLHF fine-tuning-like churn, and long-lived streams
Canary rollout: internal (2 nodes) -> staging (5 nodes) -> limited prod (10 nodes) over two weeks
Observe metrics: fragmentation_ratio, eviction_rate, bytes_moved, compaction_cpu_pct, p50/p95/p99 latencies, OOM counts
rollout_and_mitigation: Feature toggle default OFF for existing customers; enable progressively for low-risk clusters
If p99 latency increase > 5% for 15 minutes, auto-disable compaction on that cluster and notify SRE
If OOMs spike after enabling compaction, immediate rollback and capture heap profile for postmortem
Gradual ramp: start with conservative compaction quantum and increase if fragmentation remains high without latency impact
notes_for_pm: PM: prioritize canary clusters that host models with highest token churn; tie rollout to customer opt-in. Include messaging for customers about potential minor latency changes during early rollout.
